question: What is a converter dolly, as described in the manual?
choice_a: A coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel used to couple a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination
choice_b: A hydraulic jack used to raise the landing gear of a semitrailer
choice_c: A brake control valve located at the rear of the last trailer
choice_d: A device that measures rearward amplification during turns
explanation: The manual defines a converter dolly as a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor-trailer combination, forming a double bottom rig.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Coupling and Uncoupling

question: Before wheeling the converter dolly into position in front of the second (rear) trailer, how must the dolly brakes be released if the dolly has spring brakes?
choice_a: By opening the air tank petcock only
choice_b: By using the dolly parking brake control
choice_c: By disconnecting the electrical cord
choice_d: By lowering the landing gear completely
explanation: The manual states that a driver releases dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or if the dolly has spring brakes, by using the dolly parking brake control.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

question: If the distance to the converter dolly is too great to wheel it into position by hand, what does the manual say a driver can use instead?
choice_a: A forklift to lift the dolly into place
choice_b: A second driver pushing from behind
choice_c: The tractor and first semitrailer to pick up the converter dolly
choice_d: The trailer's landing gear crank
explanation: The manual states that if the distance is too great, the driver can use the tractor and first semitrailer to pick up the converter dolly.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Position Converter Dolly in Front of Second (Rear) Trailer

question: After backing the first semitrailer into position in front of the dolly tongue and hooking the dolly to the front trailer, what must be locked?
choice_a: The fifth wheel release lever
choice_b: The trailer air supply knob
choice_c: The emergency line shut-off valve
choice_d: The pintle hook
explanation: Under 'Connect Converter Dolly to Front Trailer,' the manual instructs the driver to hook the dolly to the front trailer and lock the pintle hook.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Connect Converter Dolly to Front Trailer

question: Before backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer, why must the trailer height be correct?
choice_a: So the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under, since it must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel
choice_b: So the trailer's brakes automatically release
choice_c: So the kingpin aligns with the landing gear crank
choice_d: So the electrical cord reaches the trailer socket
explanation: The manual states the trailer height must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so the trailer is raised slightly when the dolly is pushed under.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: How does the manual say a driver should test the coupling after backing the converter dolly under the rear trailer?
choice_a: By checking tire pressure on the dolly
choice_b: By pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer
choice_c: By sounding the horn twice
choice_d: By opening the emergency line shut-off valve
explanation: The manual instructs the driver to test coupling by pulling against the pin of the second semitrailer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: When making a visual check of the coupling to the rear trailer, what should the driver look for regarding the fifth wheel?
choice_a: The fifth wheel should be greased but not locked
choice_b: The fifth wheel plate should be tilted downward
choice_c: No visible space between upper and lower fifth wheel, with locking jaws closed on the kingpin
choice_d: The fifth wheel release arm should be disengaged
explanation: The manual states the visual check of coupling should confirm no space between upper and lower fifth wheel and that locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: After connecting the converter dolly to the rear trailer and raising the landing gear completely, how does the driver check for air at the rear of the second trailer?
choice_a: By listening for the parking brake to release automatically
choice_b: By checking the tire pressure gauge
choice_c: By pulling the trolley valve fully out
choice_d: By pushing the 'air supply' knob in and opening the emergency line shut-off
explanation: The manual instructs charging the trailer brakes by pushing the 'air supply' knob in, then checking for air at the rear of the second trailer by opening the emergency line shut-off, noting that if air pressure isn't there, something is wrong and the brakes won't work.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2 Connect Converter Dolly to Rear Trailer

question: Before lowering the landing gear of the second semitrailer during uncoupling of twin trailers, what two things does the manual say to do first?
choice_a: Park the rig in a straight line on firm level ground and apply parking brakes so the rig won't move
choice_b: Disconnect the electrical cord and remove the spare tire
choice_c: Release the pintle hook and drive forward slowly
choice_d: Open the service line valve and drain the air tank
explanation: The manual's uncoupling procedure begins by parking the rig in a straight line on firm level ground and applying parking brakes so the rig won't move.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: According to the manual, when should a driver chock the wheels of the second trailer during uncoupling?
choice_a: Always, regardless of brake type
choice_b: If it doesn't have spring brakes
choice_c: Only if the dolly has no landing gear
choice_d: Only when uncoupling triples, never doubles
explanation: The manual states to chock wheels of the second trailer if it doesn't have spring brakes.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: Why does the manual say to lower the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough before pulling the dolly out?
choice_a: To disconnect the safety chains automatically
choice_b: To raise the fifth wheel height
choice_c: To remove some weight from the dolly
choice_d: To align the pintle hook with the kingpin
explanation: The manual instructs lowering the landing gear of the second semitrailer enough to remove some weight from the dolly.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: After releasing the converter dolly fifth wheel latch during uncoupling, what does the manual instruct the driver to do to remove the dolly from under the rear semitrailer?
choice_a: Lower the landing gear of the first trailer
choice_b: Reverse the tractor to push the dolly out
choice_c: Disconnect the safety chains and lift the dolly by hand
choice_d: Slowly pull tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer
explanation: The manual states to slowly pull the tractor, first semitrailer, and dolly forward to pull the dolly out from under the rear semitrailer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncoupling Twin Trailers

question: What warning does the manual give about unlocking the pintle hook while uncoupling the converter dolly?
choice_a: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up and cause injury
choice_b: Never unlock the pintle hook before disconnecting the safety chains
choice_c: The pintle hook should only be unlocked while the engine is running
choice_d: The pintle hook must be unlocked before applying spring brakes
explanation: The manual warns never to unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer, because the dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury and making re-coupling difficult.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: After lowering the dolly landing gear and disconnecting the safety chains, what does the manual say to do to the converter gear before releasing the pintle hook?
choice_a: Remove the electrical cord entirely
choice_b: Apply converter gear spring brakes or chock wheels
choice_c: Fully raise the landing gear
choice_d: Open the emergency line shut-off valve
explanation: The manual instructs applying converter gear spring brakes or chocking wheels before releasing the pintle hook on the first semi-trailer.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.2 Uncouple Converter Dolly

question: According to the manual, what is the first step in coupling a triple-trailer rig?
choice_a: Couple the third trailer to the dolly first
choice_b: Attach the second trailer directly to the tractor
choice_c: Couple the tractor to the first trailer using the method already described for coupling tractor-semitrailers
choice_d: Connect all safety chains before any coupling begins
explanation: The manual states that to couple a triples rig, the driver first couples the tractor to the first trailer using the method already described for coupling tractor-semitrailers.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: How does the manual describe completing a triples rig after the tractor is coupled to the first trailer?
choice_a: By attaching the third trailer directly to the tractor's fifth wheel
choice_b: By skipping the dolly and using a rigid frame connector
choice_c: By reversing the entire rig into the third trailer
choice_d: By moving the converter dolly into position and coupling the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles
explanation: The manual explains that the driver moves the converter dolly into position and couples the first trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles, completing the triples rig.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: When uncoupling a triple-trailer rig, what does the manual say to do first?
choice_a: Uncouple the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles
choice_b: Uncouple the first trailer from the tractor
choice_c: Remove all safety chains from every trailer simultaneously
choice_d: Lower the landing gear on the tractor
explanation: The manual states that uncoupling a triple-trailer rig begins by uncoupling the third trailer by pulling the dolly out, then unhitching the dolly using the method for uncoupling doubles.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.3 Coupling and Uncoupling Triple Trailers

question: What does the manual say about coupling and uncoupling other truck-trailer and tractor-trailer combinations not specifically described?
choice_a: They all follow the exact same steps as coupling doubles
choice_b: There are too many to cover in the manual, and the driver must learn the correct way according to manufacturer and/or owner specifications
choice_c: They require a certified mechanic to perform
choice_d: They are prohibited under CDL regulations
explanation: The manual states there are too many other combinations to cover, and the driver needs to learn the correct way to couple and uncouple according to the manufacturer and/or owner specifications.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.2.4 Coupling and Uncoupling Other Combinations

question: What procedure does the manual say to use as the basis for inspecting a combination vehicle with doubles or triples?
choice_a: A simplified three-step visual scan
choice_b: The manufacturer's warranty checklist only
choice_c: The seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2
choice_d: The annual DOT inspection form
explanation: The manual instructs using the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect a combination vehicle, noting there are more things to inspect on a combination vehicle than a single vehicle.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3 Inspecting Doubles and Triples

question: When checking the lower fifth wheel during a walk-around inspection of doubles or triples, what should the locking jaws be positioned around?
choice_a: The head of the kingpin only
choice_b: The glide plate edge
choice_c: The landing gear crank
choice_d: The shank, not the head, of the kingpin
explanation: The manual specifies checking that the locking jaws are around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Coupling System Areas

question: According to the manual's checklist for double and triple trailers, how should the shut-off valve at the rear of the front trailer(s) be positioned?
choice_a: OPEN
choice_b: CLOSED
choice_c: Removed entirely
choice_d: Set to the 'emergency' position
explanation: The manual states that the shut-off valve at the rear of front trailers should be OPEN.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Double and Triple Trailers

question: According to the manual's checklist for double and triple trailers, how should the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer be positioned?
choice_a: OPEN
choice_b: CLOSED
choice_c: Half-open
choice_d: Left disconnected
explanation: The manual states that the shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer should be CLOSED.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.3.1 Additional Checks - Double and Triple Trailers

question: How does the manual say a driver should test trailer emergency brakes on doubles or triples?
choice_a: Simply listen for a hissing sound at the fifth wheel
choice_b: Disconnect the air lines and observe if the trailer rolls
choice_c: Charge the trailer air brake system, check the trailer rolls freely, then pull out the trailer air supply control (or place it in 'emergency') and pull gently on the trailer with the tractor
choice_d: Apply the parking brake and check tire tread depth
explanation: The manual describes testing trailer emergency brakes by charging the air brake system, checking the trailer rolls freely, then pulling out the trailer air supply control (or placing it in the emergency position) and pulling gently on the trailer to confirm the emergency brakes engage.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks

question: At what air pressure range does the manual say the trailer air supply control usually pops out or moves to the emergency position?
choice_a: Exactly at 100 psi
choice_b: Usually within the range of 5 to 10 psi
choice_c: Only when pressure reaches zero
choice_d: Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi
explanation: The manual states the trailer air supply control should pop out (or go from 'normal' to 'emergency') when air pressure falls into the range specified by the manufacturer, usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.
source_note: West Virginia CDL Manual, Section 7 - Doubles and Triples, 7.4.1 Additional Air Brake Checks - Test Tractor Protection Valve
